title: Man as a Rational Animal
summary: Living organisms as goal-directed, and reason as the human means of survival.

lessons.title: Life aims at itself
lessons.objective: See a living organism as an entity whose actions are directed at keeping itself alive.

exercises.prompt: In this unit, what makes an action goal-directed?

choices.text: It is the action of a living organism sustaining itself
Any motion that someone later calls a purpose
A rock rolling downhill toward a valley
A group decision about what the thing ought to want

feedback.note: Goals belong to living organisms. Their actions are organized around staying alive, not around a label added afterward.

exercises.prompt: Which of these can have a goal of its own?

choices.text: A living plant
A stone on a hillside
A cloud changing shape
An echo in a canyon

feedback.note: Only a living organism acts to maintain itself. Inanimate things change, but they do not pursue a goal.

exercises.prompt: Match each thing to what this unit says about goals.

pairs.right: Acts to sustain its own life
Has no goal of its own

feedback.note: Life is the goal that organizes a living thing's action. Nothing non-living has that kind of goal.

exercises.prompt: Complete the line about living action.

parts.text: A living organism acts to sustain its own

feedback.note: The direction of the action is the organism's own life, not a social score or a random wish.

exercises.prompt: Build the idea in order.

feedback.note: To be alive is to keep generating the action that maintains that life. It is not mere sitting still.

exercises.prompt: If an organism stops the actions that sustain it, what follows?

choices.text: Its life ends
It stays the same kind of living thing, only quieter
It becomes a more successful rock
It gains a new goal automatically

feedback.note: The goal and the process are the same fact: stop the self-sustaining action, and the organism is no longer alive.

exercises.prompt: Match the contrast.

pairs.right: Change with no aim of its own

pairs.left: The alternative for a living thing
pairs.right: Life or the end of life

feedback.note: Goal-direction is not a mood. It is the fact that the organism faces the alternative of continuing or not.

exercises.prompt: Fill the two blanks.

feedback.note: Goal-direction here means action aimed at the organism's own continued life. Inanimate things do not have it.

exercises.prompt: A river cuts a canyon over ages. On this unit's terms, the river is:

choices.text: Changing, but not pursuing a goal
A living organism sustaining itself
Choosing a moral code
Using reason as its means of survival

feedback.note: Physical change is not enough. A goal, in this unit, belongs to a living organism acting to keep itself in existence.

lessons.title: No built-in survival code
lessons.objective: Contrast automatic living action in plants and animals with the fact that a human being has no innate program for how to survive.

exercises.prompt: How does a plant keep itself alive, on this account?

choices.text: By automatic physical processes, such as taking in what its nature requires
By forming concepts and arguing about soil
By a committee of leaves
By reading a manual it wrote

feedback.note: A plant's self-sustaining action runs automatically. It does not identify the world in concepts and then decide.

exercises.prompt: What guides much of an animal's action within its range?

choices.text: Sensation and perception, within the range its body is built for
A conceptual science it invents
A written legal code
Nothing at all; animals do not act to live

feedback.note: Animals are goal-directed too, but the guidance built into sensation and perception is not the human method.

exercises.prompt: Match each kind of organism to how it sustains itself.

pairs.right: Sensation and perception in a set range

feedback.note: The ladder of living action runs from automatic processes, to perceptual guidance, to a being who must find out how to live.

exercises.prompt: Complete the contrast.

feedback.note: Nothing in human nature hands over a finished program for food, shelter, or how to act. That has to be learned.

exercises.prompt: Build the sentence about human survival.

feedback.note: Birth does not include a ready set of survival instructions. Knowledge of how to live has to be acquired.

exercises.prompt: A newborn has senses and a body. What does this unit say the newborn does not have?

choices.text: An innate set of instructions for how to survive
A body
Any contact with the world
The status of a living organism

feedback.note: The child is a living organism from the start. The means of knowing what to do is not installed as an automatic code.

exercises.prompt: Why is a human being not in the same position as a plant?

choices.text: Human survival action is not run by automatic bodily processes alone
A human being is not a living organism
A human being has no goal
Plants choose concepts and humans do not

feedback.note: Both are alive and goal-directed. The difference is the means: automatic action for the plant, no such built-in code for the human.

exercises.prompt: Match the claim to the mistake it rejects.

pairs.left: Humans lack an automatic survival code
pairs.right: Treating people as if instinct already knew how to live

pairs.left: Animals are guided within a range
pairs.right: Treating animal action as conceptual science

feedback.note: Keep the three levels apart. People are living and goal-directed, and still not pre-programmed the way a plant or a non-rational animal is.

exercises.prompt: Fill both blanks.

feedback.note: Automatic self-maintenance fits the plant. Human survival depends on knowledge that is not given at birth.

lessons.title: Reason is the means
lessons.objective: Identify reason as the human means of survival: the faculty that identifies and integrates what the senses provide.

exercises.prompt: What is the distinctively human means of survival?

choices.text: Reason
Claws and camouflage
The weather
A finished instinctive code

feedback.note: People do not survive by an automatic program or by animal equipment alone. Reason is the means that fits a rational animal.

exercises.prompt: What does reason do with what the senses provide?

choices.text: It identifies and integrates that material
It throws the senses out and starts from a blank
It substitutes a mood for observation
It takes a poll and calls the winner a fact

feedback.note: Reason is not a rival to the senses. It is the faculty that identifies and integrates the material the senses give.

exercises.prompt: Match each piece of the means of survival.

pairs.right: Guides the action that keeps you alive

feedback.note: Survival by reason is a chain: sensory material, identification, then action guided by what you know.

exercises.prompt: Name the faculty.

parts.text: Reason is the human means of

feedback.note: Reason is not an optional hobby beside life. For a human being it is how life is sustained.

exercises.prompt: Build the definition used in this lesson.

feedback.note: That is the job of reason in this unit: identify and integrate what the senses provide, so action has a guide.

exercises.prompt: Food, shelter, and tools, on this account, depend on what?

choices.text: Knowledge gained by reason and put into action
Claws humans are born with
Luck with no need to know anything
An instinct that already farms and builds

feedback.note: Producing the values a human life needs is work guided by knowledge. Reason is the basic means of that work.

exercises.prompt: Which description fits reason as a means of survival?

choices.text: The basic tool for knowing what to do in order to live
An ornament added after survival is already guaranteed
A rival that fights the fact that you are an organism
Another name for an eye or an ear

feedback.note: Eyes and ears supply material. Reason is the faculty that turns that material into knowledge you can act on.

exercises.prompt: Match the need to the role of reason.

pairs.left: What must I do to live?
Where does the material come from?

feedback.note: Reason does not float free of observation, and observation does not by itself state what you should do. Both steps belong to surviving by reason.

exercises.prompt: Fill the blanks.

feedback.note: Identification says what something is. Integration connects it with the rest of what you know. That is how reason works on sensory material.

exercises.prompt: Put the means of survival in order.

feedback.note: The order is fixed for this unit: the senses give the material, and reason integrates it into knowledge you can live by.

lessons.title: Reason has to be used
lessons.objective: Hold that reason does not run by itself: surviving by it takes the choice to think and to act on what you know.

exercises.prompt: Does reason operate automatically, the way a plant grows?

choices.text: No. It has to be used
Yes. Thinking runs whether you engage it or not
Yes, but only while you sleep
Yes, whenever a crowd feels strongly

feedback.note: The means of survival is a faculty you must exercise. It is not an automatic process like a plant's growth.

exercises.prompt: If someone refuses to think, what backup does human nature supply?

choices.text: None. There is no instinctive code waiting in reserve
Photosynthesis
A full animal survival program equal to reason
A second mind that knows without looking

feedback.note: Dropping reason does not switch on another human means of survival. The faculty you do not use does not work in your place.

exercises.prompt: Match each fact to what it requires.

pairs.left: Reason is a faculty, not a reflex
pairs.right: You have to choose to think
Does not yet sustain your life

feedback.note: Having the faculty is not the same as using it, and knowing is not the same as acting on what you know.

exercises.prompt: Complete the requirement.

parts.text: To survive by reason, you must

feedback.note: Both steps belong to the means. Thought that never guides action leaves the organism's goal unserved.

exercises.prompt: Build the warning in this lesson.

feedback.note: A capacity you never exercise is not functioning as your means of survival.

exercises.prompt: Someone memorizes that fire burns and then grabs a hot stove. What failed?

choices.text: Acting on knowledge already gained
The fact that senses exist
The fact that organisms are goal-directed
The classification of humans as animals

feedback.note: Reason serves survival when knowledge guides what you do. A fact you ignore does not protect you.

exercises.prompt: Choosing to think is required because:

choices.text: Conceptual knowledge is not produced automatically
Plants also file concepts in seed catalogs
Survival itself is optional for a living organism
Only a committee can identify a fact

feedback.note: The senses work as your contact with the world. Forming and using conceptual knowledge is something you must undertake.

exercises.prompt: Match the action to its place in survival by reason.

pairs.right: Using reason on what is there

feedback.note: Each positive step is a use of the means. Refusing the first step does not summon a substitute code.

exercises.prompt: Fill the blank.

parts.text: Reason sustains you only when it is

feedback.note: The faculty is yours by nature. Its work is not. Surviving by reason means actually thinking and acting on the result.

lessons.title: One picture of the rational animal
lessons.objective: Put the unit in one order: a goal-directed organism, no innate survival code, and reason as the means you must use.

exercises.prompt: In the phrase rational animal, what does animal mark?

choices.text: A living organism, goal-directed like other animals
A machine with no goal
A mind that is not a living being
Inanimate matter

feedback.note: The word animal keeps the human being inside life: an organism whose actions are aimed at staying alive.

exercises.prompt: In the same phrase, what does rational mark?

choices.text: Reason as the means of survival
A body covering shared with other species
An automatic code like a plant's
Whatever feeling is strongest

feedback.note: Rational names the distinctive means. The organism lives by identifying and integrating the world, then acting on that knowledge.

exercises.prompt: Match each part of the unit to its idea.

pairs.right: Survival is not programmed in advance
Thinking and acting are not automatic

feedback.note: Those four points are the whole unit. Each one answers a different question about the same being.

exercises.prompt: Complete the definition's two sides.

feedback.note: Rational names the means. Animal names the living, goal-directed organism. Neither word is a spare decoration.

exercises.prompt: Build the order this unit uses.

feedback.note: Start from the living organism, then the missing automatic code, then reason as the means that fills that need.

exercises.prompt: Which order matches this unit?

choices.text: Goal-directed life, no innate code, reason as the means you must use
Reason first, and life only if a committee approves it
Humans photosynthesize, then optionally think
Rocks have goals, and organisms copy them

feedback.note: Reason is the means because you are a living organism without an automatic code. The order is not optional.

exercises.prompt: Which claim leaves the unit?

choices.text: Reason is a weekend hobby after instinct has already secured your life
Living organisms act to sustain themselves
Humans have no automatic survival code
Reason identifies and integrates sensory material

feedback.note: Instinct does not already solve human survival. Reason is the means, and it works only when it is used.

exercises.prompt: Match the question to the unit's answer.

pairs.left: What kind of thing has goals here?
What do humans lack at birth?
What is their means of survival?

feedback.note: Three questions, three answers. Together they state what a rational animal is.

exercises.prompt: Close the unit.

parts.text: Reason is the means by which a human

feedback.note: That is the unit in one line: a living, goal-directed organism, surviving by reason rather than by an innate code.

exercises.prompt: State the means in a full line.

feedback.note: Keep the summary in that shape. Reason is not an extra. It is how this organism lives.
